subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student with severe exam anxiety is gradually and repeatedly exposed to increasingly exam-like situations (first just thinking about the exam, then sitting in the exam room, then attempting a practice test) while practising relaxation techniques at each step, until the fear response fades. This behaviour-therapy technique is called:
explanation: Systematic desensitisation (developed by Joseph Wolpe) pairs relaxation with a gradual, step-by-step hierarchy of exposure to the feared stimulus — distinct from flooding (intense, immediate exposure to the full feared situation without gradual buildup) or aversion therapy (pairing an unwanted behaviour with an unpleasant stimulus to reduce it).
